Type.rationale: `public override CardType Type => TinkerTimeType` (MadScience.cs:80) == the sim's instance attribute, written by `configure(tinker_type, rider)` alongside `self.tinker_type`. The default of ATTACK matches the canonical constructor (MadScience.cs:167-170).

TargetType.rationale: `TinkerTimeType != CardType.Attack ? TargetType.Self : TargetType.AnyEnemy` (MadScience.cs:82-92) == `TargetType.ANY_ENEMY if tinker_type == CardType.ATTACK else TargetType.SELF`.

GainsBlock.maps_to: NOT PORTED -- `gains_block` is left at its False class default (mad_science.py:92-97)
GainsBlock.issue: `public override bool GainsBlock => TinkerTimeType == CardType.Skill` (MadScience.cs:94) is TYPE-DEPENDENT, and the sim never sets `gains_block` at all -- not in the class body and not in `configure` (mad_science.py:114-125, which sets `card_type`, `target_type` and `rider` but not this). So a Skill-configured Mad Science, which gains 8 block, reports `gains_block = False`. Observable through the Nimble enchantment, whose `can_enchant` gates on exactly this flag (cards/base.py:65-69 names Nimble as the reader): in the game Nimble accepts a Skill Mad Science and in the sim it refuses. DORMANT only if Nimble is unreachable -- it is a ported enchantment (enchantments.py), and Mad Science reaches the deck from the ported Tinker Time event, so this is LIVE for the Skill configuration. Note the sim DOES get the related `base_block` right, via an overriding property that returns the block only for the Skill type (mad_science.py:131-133) -- so the type-dependence was clearly understood and this one flag was missed.

PortraitPath.rationale: Per-type card art path selection (MadScience.cs:69, 172-187). Presentation.

AllPortraitPaths.rationale: The three per-type art paths, used for asset preloading (MadScience.cs:73-78). Presentation.

ctor.rationale: `base(1, CardType.Attack, CardRarity.Event, TargetType.AnyEnemy, shouldShowInCardLibrary: false)` (MadScience.cs:167-170) == cost 1 / ATTACK / EVENT / ANY_ENEMY defaults. `shouldShowInCardLibrary: false` is a compendium-UI flag with no sim counterpart and no gameplay effect. `configure` then overwrites type and target.

CanonicalVars.rationale: All ELEVEN C# vars are accounted for (MadScience.cs:96-109), which makes this the most var-dense card in the pool: DamageVar 12 -> `_damage`, BlockVar 8 -> `_block`, and the nine rider amounts as module constants with matching values -- SappingWeak 2, SappingVulnerable 2, ViolenceHits 3, ChokingDamage 6, EnergizedEnergy 2, WisdomCards 3, ExpertiseStrength 2, ExpertiseDexterity 2, CuriousReduction 1 (mad_science.py:66-75). The two printed vars are exposed through overriding `base_damage` / `base_block` properties that return them only for the matching type (128-133), which is more faithful than a plain attribute would be. The rider constants are module-level rather than instance vars, so `magic_number` does not surface them -- acceptable, since C# keys them by name rather than treating any one as the card's headline number.

OnPlay.issue: The type dispatch, every rider effect and every amount are faithful, and the rider-per-type partition is correct: C# handles Expertise/Curious/Improvement inside `ExecutePower` (MadScience.cs:232-248) and Sapping/Choking/Energized/Wisdom/Chaos in `ExecuteRider` (267-294), which the sim reorganises into `_play_attack` (sapping, choking), `_play_skill` (energized, wisdom, chaos) and `_play_power` (expertise, curious, improvement) -- the same nine effects, and `configure` enforces the per-type rider partition (mad_science.py:117-118) that C# leaves to Tinker Time. The Violence hit count is right (3 vs 1, MadScience.cs:218). The Chaos rider even gets the RNG STREAM right, branching on `crng.is_parity` and using `crng.card_gen` (mad_science.py:184-188) -- the correct shape that card/discovery, card/distraction, card/jack_of_all_trades, card/jackpot, card/metamorphosis and card/hidden_gem all miss. THE DIVERGENCE is the sim's two extra liveness guards: `if target.is_gone or ctx.player.is_dead: break` between the Violence hits (151-152) and `if target.is_gone: return` before the Sapping / Choking riders (154-155). The per-hit break is the correct analogue of AttackCommand's own breaks and carries nothing; the RIDER guard does. C# applies the power unconditionally and the only gate is `Creature.CanReceivePowers` (Creature.cs:308-321), whose doc comment states that DEAD creatures can still receive powers -- it refuses only for a REMOVED corpse. The two agree for an ordinary kill (`CreatureCmd.Damage` runs `Kill` before returning, CreatureCmd.cs:409, and removal happens at 523-525) and diverge for a corpse whose removal was VETOED (`ShouldCreatureBeRemovedFromCombatAfterDeath`, CreatureCmd.cs:508; the sim's `retained_after_death`, cmds.py:100-104), because `is_gone` is `is_dead or escaped` (creatures.py:44-46). Observable through ViciousPower and any listener that fires on a power landing regardless of target liveness. Same mechanism and same verdict as card/bash's OnPlay entry (rule 3); LIVE. One more nuance recorded rather than verdicted: the Chaos rider uses `set_free_this_turn` where C# calls `SetToFreeThisTurn()` (MadScience.cs:287) -- the same verb -- and adds to hand via `add_to_hand` where C# uses `CardPileCmd.Add(cardModel, PileType.Hand)` (288), the pile-verb difference the creature_card_cmds seam owns.

OnUpgrade.rationale: `AddKeyword(CardKeyword.Innate)` (MadScience.cs:252) == `self.innate = True`, and this card DOES re-seed the flag in `_init_vars` (`self.innate = False`, mad_science.py:109, with a comment saying why), so `downgrade()` restores it -- `py audit/tools/card_probes.py downgrade` does not list mad_science. The correct pattern, unlike card/aggression, card/hello_world and card/juggling.

AddExtraArgsToDescription.rationale: `description.Add("CardType", ...)` plus one boolean per rider (MadScience.cs:255-265) feeds the localisation template that renders the card text. Presentation.

guards.what: the sim adds `can_be_generated_by_modifiers = False` (mad_science.py:97), which MadScience.cs does not override
guards.rationale: Inert: the flag gates the random-CURSE pool and Mad Science is an Event-rarity Attack/Skill/Power, not a curse. Same inert extra as card/byrdonis_egg and card/lantern_key.
